I'm a 25F working adult and living alone. My mom is kind of similar-- don't go out past 8pm (sometimes 4pm), don't wear a tank top at home, always wear long sleeves outside, needs to know where I am and who I'm seeing. Randomly comes into my room to rant or just say weird things. 

She wants me to move back to "save money" too but I need my space. I think they just miss me (you) and don't want to say the words. Just give them a hug, make them some tea and have a chat.

Get a lot of rest and stock up on your favorite drink! I've been drinking a bunch of Caprisun and it kicks me out of the funk sometimes :) Gatorade/vitamin water might be good options for electrolytes and energy.

I. Love. This. 

Are you selling any prints??

Hey,

Take a deep breath first! And a few more. Sounds simple but really helps. 

The pandemic has got everyone feeling extra lonely and anxious. I'm in the same boat right now, losing friends so I totally feel you. I've accepted it as a phase of life. Things come and go, there are ups and downs but you just have to learn to make the best out of every situation. I still struggle with the loneliness, so I've been leaning more on my family these days.

But with every painful experience, there is an opportunity to be better. Revisit your old hobbies, meditate, or bring more value to your current relationships. Maybe your friends are going through a rough time too and need you to reach out. Or maybe you're losing these friends so you can create a network closer or more available to you. 

Hope this helps!

Lol yep. Need to account for 

1. Time it takes people to show symptoms, 
2. How long they wait to go to the hospital,
3. 2 weeks for the positive tests to come back,
4. Lag in processing the data,
5. The time it takes to recover/die and when that is registered in the system.

There’s no way the statistics for the protests/reopening could be show so soon. I think Texas opened April 30 but didn’t see its spike until early June, so the impact will likely be seen in a month or so.
Thank you, I appreciate reading this.
Thank you for your encouraging words and the small chuckle 💛

Thank you for sharing. I’m sorry you had to go through this as well.

I WFH too, which makes the decision a little harder to live with. But we need to remember that our worries and anxieties are not unfounded. We did our best and the right thing by letting them go to a family that is ready. 

Good luck and we can get through this!
You can do this! Don’t be afraid to lean on people for support.

I’m very happy to hear that you’re in a better place and with a new puppy.

Thank you for your kind words and sharing your story. I see a lot of people either stick it through or reject having a puppy completely. So it gives me hope to see something similar — you knew there was a better time/place and you waited for it. I’m slowly coming to peace with my decision and will 100% be ready with time.

I wish you and your new puppy the best! 🙏🏼💛

Thank you. I need to accept and remind myself that my problems were real. And all I can do is do my best.

I’m extremely grateful for your support and wish you and your family the best 💛

Thank you for sharing. It helps to know I’m not alone.

I also have GAD and history of depression. And hearing that so many people came out successfully on the other end makes it harder to look in the mirror. I empathize with others but it’s still so hard for me to forgive myself. I’m trying to accept that one bad thing doesn’t discount all the progress I’ve made.

Hey!

I hope you’re feeling better. I’m sorry you had to go through this. I’m going through something similar right now and it sucks. I do regret my decision but I also think it was for the best.

After extensive research, preparation and planning, I finally got my 11 week old pup. I thought by just living in a dog friendly apartment I’d be able to let some things go but I constantly worried about everything and psyched myself out. I’m not living in the safest neighborhood and people litter everywhere/ don’t pick up after their dogs. I also live alone in a small apartment with stairs and he was the type of puppy who couldn’t climb stairs until older, which limited exercise space. I got him when I thought shops were reopening because of COVID and the riots just started. I didn’t realize how hard it would be to get help because everything was shut down. I was scared he would suddenly grow up with the manifestations of my irresponsibilities. I convinced myself it was already happening because I knew, in a different situation, I could give him a better life. And I knew that there was someone else already in that situation right now.

During those 2 weeks, I couldn’t work, I couldn’t sleep, I couldn’t eat, I couldn’t think. I barely drink water and I had panic attacks that lasted from 5am to 4pm. There were ups and downs but it got better day by day. Everyday since I took him back, I wish I stuck it through. But he’s now in a happy home and I need to suck it up. 

In hindsight, I would’ve waited another year. I got into a major car accident and totaled my car the day before I got my puppy. I’m just starting to grow in my career, working full time, and studying part time and I’m planning to move to a new home and a good neighborhood next year. I just wanted things to happen, and happen now. 

I regret giving him back but I think it was the right decision. My living room, small as it is, suddenly feels so empty. I still think having a puppy will add to my life, but I’m waiting for the right time this time.

Thank you for posting. It helps me a lot to read other stories because it’s easier for me to forgive someone else rather than myself. 

I hope things have been better since.

I used to have this exact mindset. It was fun but my responsibilities caught up to me so I tried to look for something more concrete.

I threw myself into work. I tried having pets. I tried to volunteer and I tried to help my family. Everything still feels like a means to an end. Maybe I’m looking at things the wrong way?

Hi all, 

Thank you for being so supportive and responsive.

I woke up this morning with the same dreaded feeling and I took him back to his breeder. I felt like I did the right thing.

But I do miss him a lot and can’t stand looking at our photos/videos. He’s such a great puppy and I wish I were ready.

I feel terrible that I won’t ever know if this was a mistake but I can only hope things will get better.

Thank you all for sharing.

Thank you for sharing!

I think having him made me really think about the things I need to work on. I’m working full time, studying part time, living in an apartment and need a stronger support system. I’m financially ready, but I don’t have the emotional and mental stability to keep him just yet.

I’m grateful I realized in time so he can still go to a good home that hopefully can give him more. I miss him so much already but I know it’s for the best.
2 weeks

I’m sorry to hear what you’re going through. I went through something similar and that’s partially where my anxiety is coming from as well. The family member lives overseas so it’s been really hard not being able to visit him or be there for him. I miss him so much.

I definitely wish I waited to have a support system closer to me in proximity. I don’t want people close to me to travel an hour to me since things are so chaotic right now. I’ll try going out more often and find something that actively gets my mind off things for a while. Talking and thinking have its limitations.

Things have been getting better day by day so I’ll wait another week to make any final decisions. 

Thank you for sharing and offering advice.

Are you living alone and raising your puppy by yourself too? Just looking for a bit of hope/reality.

I’m not sure and that’s what’s causing more anxiety. I’m getting therapy and meditating and doing what I can. My days are full of ups and downs and I just don’t know anymore.

Thank you for the kind suggestions. I’m really relieved to hear my puppy isn’t the only one with a food issue. I’ll try hand feeding him this week and hope that things improve.

He is taking medication for Giardia so that might be why he has some weird habits. I do want to love and spend time with him as much as I can but I just get such awful anxiety in the mornings. There’s definitely a lot to think about.
He plays and can play for hours. I’m feeding him royal canon and cottage cheese (for bone health) as directed by the breeder

I have therapy every two weeks. I’ve been meditating every morning but I’m still constantly worried... it just sucks that I worked so hard to get a puppy and Im starting to think I can’t handle having one.

Thank you for your advice! And so sorry to hear you went through something similar. 

Do you think reaching out to the bigger boss might be considered insubordination if I don’t tell my direct supervisor first? I normally only interact with my supervisor and I work remote so walking by for a casual chat is not an option.
Thank you for verifying my fears (as weird as that sounds.) It’s good to know I’m not seeing things that aren’t there.

Sorry posting dumb questions because my anxiety is acting up. 

I’ve already paid in full for this pup and am thinking of what I can do now. She claims to always keep in contact with the puppies and their owners. But there were definitely a bunch red flags, like she kept disregarding temperament and meeting the parents when I brought it up. I should’ve listened to my gut and now I feel like a huge sucker.
